answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a small deposit in a shared kernel contract before it can transact, with the stake slashed if peers prove fake identities. Reputation then accrues slowly like a terrace built level by level, so a flood of new accounts cannot instantly outweigh established agents. An ocean of cheap identities is worthless when every identity must lock real value and earn trust gradually, making mass fakery expensive and easy to detect.
